original_question: Let p be a prime, and P a finite p-group. (a) Suppose that P has an abelian subgroup of order pn. For which n does P necessarily have a normal abelian subgroup of order pn? (b) Suppose that P has an elementary abelian subgroup of order pn. For which n does P necessarily have a normal elementary abelian subgroup of order pn? It is easy to see that for p = 2, the answer to(b) is “yes” only for n = 1. The answer to both questions is “yes” for n < (p + 2)/2(G. G. Glauberman, J. Algebra, 319, no. 2(2008), 800–805), as well as for n ⩽ 5 when p ̸= 2(M. Konvisser, D. Jonah, J. Algebra, 34(1975), 309–330). The answer to both questions is “no” for n ⩾ (p+9)/2 when p ⩾ 5(for p ⩾ 7 due to G. Glauberman, Contemp. Math., 524(2010), 61–65; for p = 3, 5 due to Ya. G. Berkovich, J. Algebra, 248, no. 2(2002), 472–553). Thus, the only open cases for p ⩾ 5 are n = 6 for p = 5, and n = (p + 3)/2, (p + 5)/2, (p + 7)/2 for p > 5.
target_in_paper: Problem 21.51 in the section New Problems (21st issue, 2026): determine for which integers n the existence, in a finite p-group, of an abelian subgroup of order p^n or an elementary abelian subgroup of order p^n forces a normal subgroup of the same type and order.
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper's exact target. It matches Problem 21.51 almost verbatim: the hypotheses are the same (p prime, P a finite p-group), the two parts are the same (abelian versus elementary abelian subgroups of order p^n), and the summary of known positive and negative ranges and remaining open cases is the same as in the paper.
missing_details: Make the universal quantifier explicit: for a fixed prime p and integer n >= 1, the property is required to hold for every finite p-group P with the stated subgroup.
State explicitly that the goal is to determine all such integers n, possibly as a function of p.
Spell out that elementary abelian of order p^n means a subgroup isomorphic to (C_p)^n.

To be fully paper-faithful as a stand-alone question, include the current reduction recorded in Problem 21.51: for p >= 5 the unresolved cases are p = 5, n = 6, and p > 5 with n = (p+3)/2, (p+5)/2, (p+7)/2; also, for p = 2 in part (b), the answer is yes only for n = 1.

If historical context is mentioned, distinguish the exact target Problem 21.51 from the earlier weaker predecessor Problem 16.33, where normality is only required in the normal closure <B^G>, and from Archive problem 15.24, which records a sufficiently-large-p variant.
refined_question: Fix a prime p. Determine all integers n >= 1 such that, for every finite p-group P, the following implication holds: if P contains an abelian subgroup of order p^n, then P contains a normal abelian subgroup of order p^n; and if P contains an elementary abelian subgroup of order p^n (that is, a subgroup isomorphic to (C_p)^n), then P contains a normal elementary abelian subgroup of order p^n. In the status recorded in Problem 21.51, this amounts to settling the remaining unresolved cases: p = 5 with n = 6, and p > 5 with n = (p+3)/2, (p+5)/2, or (p+7)/2; moreover, for p = 2 in the elementary-abelian case, the implication holds only for n = 1.
justification: The exact target is Problem 21.51, not a broader neighboring question. Your draft already captures its two-part classification problem and reproduces the paper's status summary. The refinements above only make explicit the hidden quantifiers, the meaning of elementary abelian, and the fact that the paper itself narrows the unresolved cases to a short list. Problem 16.33 is an earlier and weaker predecessor for small primes, and Archive problem 15.24 records a related solved large-p phenomenon, so they are useful for context but should not replace Problem 21.51 as the target.
